You: Can you give me the command line to:
The command to redirect port 22 of a machine accessible on 192.168.2.72 using SSH would be:

`ssh -L 2222:192.168.2.72:22 <username>@<remote_machine>`

Replace `<username>` and `<remote_machine>` with the actual username and remote machine you want to connect to.

This command will create a local port forwarding from your local machine's port 2222 to the remote machine's port 22, allowing you to access the remote machine's SSH server as if it were running on your local machine.
You: In ssh how to specify port to conne:
When connecting to a remote machine using SSH and the default port (22) is not being used, you can specify the port number to use by appending the port number to the hostname or IP address.

For example:

* `ssh user@host:port` - Connects to the host on the specified port.
* `ssh user@192.168.2.72:2222` - Connects to 192.168.2.72 on port 2222.

Alternatively, you can use the `-p` option followed by the port number:

* `ssh -p port user@host` - Connects to the host on the specified port.
* `ssh -p 2222 user@192.168.2.72` - Connects to 192.168.2.72 on port 2222.

In both cases, replace "user" with your actual username and "host" or "IP address" with the actual hostname or IP address you want to connect to.
You: Is there an option to add in order:
Yes, there is an option to prevent SSH from opening a graphical session when forwarding a port. You can use the `-X` or `--no-x11-forwarding` option to disable X11 forwarding.

Here's how you can do it:

* `ssh -L 2222:192.168.2.72:22 -X user@remote_machine`
* `ssh -L 2222:192.168.2.72:22 --no-x11-forwarding user@remote_machine`

By using this option, SSH will not open a graphical session when forwarding the port, and you can still access the remote machine's SSH server as if it were running on your local machine.

Note that you can combine these options with other SSH options to customize your connection further.
